speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please tell me, how long have you had these symptoms and how did the skin lesions appear?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, RF, ANA, and HLA-B27.
REQUEST IMAGES: Wrist_Xray, Knee_Xray, Skin_Lesions_photo.
The recent self-resolving knee pain and your camping trip in Minnesota suggest a possible infection like Lyme disease or a reactive arthritis, so we need to see if there is joint swelling or specific rash patterns.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Erythema Migrans) with associated monoarthritis/reactive arthritis.
